method: Fetched current GitHub run, attempt-1 jobs, artifact list, each artifact metadata and all seven ZIP byte streams through the authenticated read-only API; checked ZIP size and SHA-256 against GitHub metadata.

Read all 56 retained tgz byte streams directly inside the ZIPs; checked size/SHA-256 against the fixed-head committed audit, and SHA-512 against staging verifier inventories and installed optional lock records.

Read package manifests and native BUILD/package-manifest/binary/notice members; checked positive names, versions, OS/CPU/libc, provenance byte lengths, SHA-256 and modes. Independently resolved the three audited Git trees at candidate merge, direct head and consumer checkout.

Checked each normal example report against the expected source scopes, function assessments, mutation counts and toolVersion 0.19.0; checked worker 1/2 parity records, phase-completion logs, thresholds and successful identity steps.
Inspected fixed-head workflow and verifier source to identify assertions whose raw inputs are not retained; checked Alpine job logs for pinned image digests and Node download checksum success.
limits: This is retained-evidence verification, not an independent rerun of seven operating systems.

Raw workers=2 assessment JSON, installed project package.json/package-lock.json, installed directories and Windows shim bytes are not retained. Worker parity, root dependency/optional flags, exclusive native selection, package versions, source/link preservation and exit codes are supported by inspected verifier assertions completing successfully; the retained normal reports, optional-lock summaries and binary hashes were checked directly.

Staging for Alpine runs on the Linux runner before Docker; expectedTarget is null there. The consumption job runs in the pinned native Alpine image, validates the musl runtime before verification, and rejects rustc/cargo on PATH. Reports do not contain a separate libc or complete installed-tool inventory.

The Windows staging manifest field contains only release-notice-audit.json because its path-portability fallback keeps the basename; candidate, coordinates, source trees and all archive hashes still match the fixed-head committed audit.

The audited package builds use merge commit 6c2e27796c094e2ac50fe5e2665cd39c55cb7bc1 from direct head 0996b5401b7ae9cbdb73f8062a317692e8a65711. Consumption uses 0aca064d4f92b529c49fe0f81d8d08f761b4668c; only crates/packages/packaging source-tree equivalence is claimed.

No npm registry installation or publication was performed. These results do not establish current browser CI success, merge readiness, support for other versions/runtimes, or npm registry availability.
